correctness.rationale: For every valid supporting normal, nonnegative outward component follows from the last feasible exit and the rolling interior ball. The relaxed halfspace maximizer lies on the tangent plane at tangential distance t=sqrt(s²-tau² a²)-tau b in [0,s], with degenerate normal-only cases also bounded by s. Projection onto the tangent ball preserves the local radius, and its displacement equals sqrt(rho²+||p-q||²)-rho. Cauchy--Schwarz gives the uniform inequality. The disk witness with b=epsilon³ realizes asymptotic ratio one and a unique relaxed maximizer. Packaged checker passes 3,000 planar numerical cases and seven sharpness instances; proof is symbolic and dimension independent.

value.rationale: The original one-tangent local LMO is a concrete optimization subroutine whose proved additive quadratic constant enters the geometric term of the local-oracle convergence transfer. The result improves that coefficient from 2/rho to an optimal 1/(2rho) for the identical routine, a factor-four strengthening, and shows that even for the disk no higher-order uniform accuracy is possible. It does not assert improvements to all implementations, the order of outer convergence, or wall-clock time.
